note: Owner-authored identity overrides for the R15-R19 catch-up (owner ruling 2026-07-20) and, from 2026-08-30, the finals weeks. These resolve export display names that do NOT cleanly map to a single active stable identity, BY STABLE KEY and never by display name or row order. Values are store `key`s. Applied BEFORE the name resolver; a covered name with no matching rule is treated as UNRESOLVED (halt), never guessed.
identity_model_note: THREE DISTINCT IDENTITY CONCEPTS (corrective 2026-07-20, review directive G) — do not conflate them: (1) STABLE KEY — the store `key` (e.g. bailey-williams-wb); the ONLY thing a score attaches to. (2) AFL CLUB — the real football club the player plays for, store field `afl_club` (e.g. Western Bulldogs). (3) AFFL OWNERSHIP TEAM — the AFFL fantasy/ownership team, store field `affl_team` (e.g. Collingwood Magpies). Prior notes mislabelled Bailey Williams as 'Collingwood' and Bailey J. Williams as 'Sydney' — those are AFFL ownership teams, NOT the players' AFL clubs. The score-to-key MAPPINGS below are unchanged; only the descriptive club/team text is corrected.

Williams — AFL club West Coast (afl_club); AFFL ownership team Sydney Swans (affl_team): R16=67, R17=82, R18=100, R19=84. (The AFL clubs are Western Bulldogs and West Coast; Collingwood and Sydney are the AFFL ownership teams, not the players' clubs.)  ||  R20 ADDENDUM (owner ruling 2026-07-28, ITEM 208): R20=87 -> bailey-williams-wb added. The R20 export writes the two players APART ('Bailey Williams' 87 and 'Bailey J. Williams' 80), matching the store display names exactly, so the bare ActivePoolResolver resolves both unaided; this rule intercepts the name BEFORE the resolver (round_catchup.py:85-92) and therefore HALTED R20 as override-unmapped until this line was added. The seam has since measured that ZERO display names in the store are shared by two active players — the collision this rule patches was a FootyWire export artifact that the owner's current export no longer produces. This mapping therefore carries a STANDING COST (one hand-added line per round, forever) with no remaining justification. Retiring or round-scoping this rule is filed as the first act after R20 lands (owner word 2026-07-28); it is sequenced behind R20 only because changing course mid-flight costs more than it saves.
overrides.r22_note: R22 RE-ENGAGED FOR ONE ROUND — owner ruling 2026-08-10. The R22 export REGRESSED to the pre-R20 shape: it writes BOTH players under the single bare display name 'Bailey Williams' (97 and 89), instead of the R20/R21 shape that wrote them apart as 'Bailey Williams' and 'Bailey J. Williams'. With the rule scoped out of R22 the bare ActivePoolResolver sends BOTH rows to bailey-williams-wb, which the catch-up preflight correctly HALTED as a duplicate stable-key assignment (verified: preflight run 2026-08-10 on store 37ced3ce, sole halt reason). Nothing in the export or in the store distinguishes the two scores, so the ingestion seat refused to guess and put the question to the owner. HIS WORD, VERBATIM: '97 = West Coast, 89 = Bulldogs'. Recorded here as the (round, score) mapping below: 22|97 -> bailey-williams-wc (Bailey J. Williams, AFL club West Coast), 22|89 -> bailey-williams-wb (Bailey Williams, AFL club Western Bulldogs). The owner's score FILE IS UNTOUCHED (scores/R22.csv is byte-identical to the couriered file, md5 82b456d5675c18b137180416b82432fc) — the ruling lives here, in the identity record, not in the data. The retirement of this rule stands for every round where the export writes the two players apart; R22 is a one-round re-engagement forced by the export, not a reversal of the R20 retirement. If future exports keep collapsing the two names, the standing cost returns and the rule should be re-argued rather than hand-extended each week.
overrides.retired_note: ROUND-SCOPED TO R15-R19 AND RETIRED FROM R20 ONWARD — owner word 2026-07-28, ITEM 208. The collision this rule existed for no longer occurs: the export now writes the two players apart ('Bailey Williams' and 'Bailey J. Williams'), matching the store exactly, and a re-measurement on store e3aaba77 found ZERO display names shared by two or more active players across all 804 — both raw and under the resolver's normalisation. From R20 the name goes to the live ActivePoolResolver like any other and resolves unaided to bailey-williams-wb. KEPT for R15-R19 rather than deleted because those fixtures genuinely do list both players under the single display name 'Bailey Williams', and the catch-up proofs re-run them; deleting the rule would silently misattribute historical rounds. The R20 mapping '20|87' that was hand-added on 2026-07-28 has been removed with this scoping — it was the one round the rule taxed before it was retired, and the identity it produced (bailey-williams-wb) is exactly what the bare resolver produces, so nothing in the applied round changes.

overrides.name: Bailey Williams WBD
overrides.reason: R23 — owner ruling 2026-08-20. The R23 export writes the two Bailey Williams players APART, but it decorates one of them with a club suffix the store does not carry: 'Bailey Williams WBD' (69) alongside 'Bailey J. Williams' (125). 'Bailey J. Williams' matches the store display name exactly and resolves unaided to bailey-williams-wc (AFL club West Coast). 'Bailey Williams WBD' matches NOTHING: the store's display name is the bare 'Bailey Williams', and the normaliser strips punctuation and case but does not delete the token 'WBD'. The read-only R23 preflight measured this as the ONE genuinely unresolved name in the file. THE OWNER'S WORD, VERBATIM: 'the one that isn't Bailey J Williams' — i.e. WBD is the Western Bulldogs Bailey, stable key bailey-williams-wb. THIS IS A NEW ENTRY, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THE RULE ABOVE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The runbook's §3 step-2 remediation recipe says to add 23 to overrides['Bailey Williams'].applies_to_rounds plus a '23|69' map line; that recipe DOES NOT WORK on this file and was simulated failing. IdentityOverrides._by_name is keyed by the EXACT display string the export writes (round_catchup.py:71, resolve() does _by_name.get(name) on the raw name), so the 'Bailey Williams' rule is never consulted for a row that says 'Bailey Williams WBD'. Extending it would have left the name unresolved and halted the advance. It also honours H5 rather than violating it: the R20 retirement of the bare-name rule STANDS — this file does not collapse the two names, so the old collision does not recur and the old rule is correctly left out of scope for R23. What is needed is a new NAME, and it is round-scoped to [23] so it carries no standing weekly cost; if the export keeps writing the suffix, the rule should be re-argued rather than hand-extended each week. There is no bare 'Bailey Williams' row in the R23 file, so this binding creates NO duplicate stable key. The owner's score FILE IS UNTOUCHED (scores/R23.csv is byte-identical to the couriered file, md5 f4849bc4933801e80228bfc0e29e0c65) — the ruling lives here, in the identity record, not in the data.

All listed 'Will Hayes' scores attach to will-hayes-b.
